title: Travel Collocations and Fixed Phrases
grammarTitle: Travel Collocations — Words That Go Together
grammarNote: Коллокации (collocations) — слова, которые часто сочетаются вместе в английском языке. В теме путешествий есть свои устойчивые сочетания, которые нужно запомнить как единицы. Не "make a ticket" — а "buy a ticket". Не "do a trip" — а "go on a trip". Изучение коллокаций делает речь естественной.

grammarTable.subject: book
grammarTable.verb: book + accommodation / a room / a flight / a ticket / a table
grammarTable.example: "Book a hotel room." / "Book a flight to Almaty." / "Book in advance."

grammarTable.subject: catch
grammarTable.verb: catch + a bus / train / flight / taxi
grammarTable.example: "Did you catch the 9 o'clock train?" / "We need to catch our flight."

grammarTable.subject: miss
grammarTable.verb: miss + a bus / train / flight / connection
grammarTable.example: "I missed the train by two minutes." / "Don't miss your connection."

grammarTable.subject: go on
grammarTable.verb: go on + a trip / a journey / holiday / a tour / an excursion
grammarTable.example: "We went on a day trip to Charyn." / "She's going on holiday."

grammarTable.subject: check in/out
grammarTable.example: "Check in is at 2 p.m." / "We checked out at 11." (hotel/airport)

grammarTable.subject: get
grammarTable.verb: get + a visa / a passport / a ticket / to a place
grammarTable.example: "Get a visa for Europe." / "How do I get to the station?"

rows.example: "Book a ROOM / FLIGHT / TICKET / TABLE / TOUR / HOSTEL." ✅ NOT "make a reservation" (formal) and NOT "do a booking."
"Take a TRAIN / BUS / TAXI / FLIGHT / BOAT." ✅ "Take a taxi to the airport." / "We took the overnight train."
"Catch a BUS / TRAIN / FLIGHT." ✅ Suggests urgency — you might miss it! "Run — we need to catch the bus!"
"Miss a BUS / TRAIN / FLIGHT / CONNECTION." ✅ "She missed the train by two minutes." — it left without her.

rows.form: GO ON: go on + journey type
rows.example: "Go on a TRIP / TOUR / EXCURSION / HOLIDAY / SAFARI." ✅ NOT "go on a travel" — "travel" is a verb here.
"Get TO a place (arrive)" / "Get AROUND a city (move around)." ✅ "How do I get to the station?"
"I travel light — just a backpack." = with as little luggage as possible.
"We went somewhere off the beaten track." = not a typical tourist destination.
"Make the most of your time in Almaty." = use your time as well as possible.
"Pack your bags — we leave at 7!" = put everything in your luggage.
"We set off early in the morning." = begin a journey.
"Arrive IN a city." / "Arrive AT the station / airport." (specific point = at)

grammarExtra.title: Arrive in vs arrive at vs arrive to

rows.example: "We arrived IN Almaty at midnight." / "She arrived IN Kazakhstan last week." ✅
"He arrived AT the airport." / "She arrived AT the hotel." ✅ (specific place)
✗ "We arrived TO Almaty." — NEVER "arrive to"! ✅ "arrive IN" or "arrive AT".
"When did you get TO Almaty?" — informal equivalent of "arrive in/at". ✅
✅ "GO ON a trip." — "make" doesn't collocate with "trip."
✅ "GO ON a journey." or "MAKE a journey" (formal). NOT "do."
✅ "arrive IN Almaty." — cities take "in", not "to".
✅ "take a flight" / "catch a flight" / "book a flight." NOT "travel a flight."

grammarTip:
Travel collocations — главные сочетания:

BOOK: a room, a flight, a ticket, a hostel, a tour
TAKE: a bus, a train, a taxi, a flight (как добраться)
CATCH: a bus, a train (успеть / не опоздать)
MISS: a flight, a connection, a train (опоздать)
GO ON: a trip, a holiday, an excursion, a tour
GET TO: как добраться ("How do I get to...?")

⚠️ Ловушки:
✗ "arrive to Almaty" → ✅ "arrive IN Almaty"
✗ "make a trip" → ✅ "go ON a trip"
✗ "travel a flight" → ✅ "take / book a flight"

Fixed phrases:
"travel light" / "set off early" / "make the most of"
"pack your bags" / "off the beaten track"

exercises.text: She ___ a hotel room three weeks in advance.
exercises.hint: "BOOK a hotel room." ✅ "Book" is the correct verb for reservations — not "make" or "do."

exercises.text: We ___ a day trip to Charyn Canyon last weekend.
exercises.hint: "GO ON a day trip." ✅ "went on" = past of "go on." You go on trips, holidays, excursions.
Cities → "arrive IN." "We arrived IN Shymkent." ✅ NEVER "arrive to Shymkent."

exercises.text: Hurry — we're going to ___ the last bus!
exercises.hint: "MISS the bus." ✅ = the bus leaves without you. "miss" = fail to catch transport.

exercises.text: "We need to ___ a taxi — the flight leaves in 40 minutes!"
exercises.hint: "CATCH a taxi" (suggests urgency) ✅ / "TAKE a taxi" (neutral) ✅ — both collocate with "taxi." With urgency, "catch" is more natural.

exercises.text: "We ___ early — at 5 a.m. — to catch the first train."
exercises.hint: "SET OFF" = begin a journey. "We SET OFF at 5 a.m." ✅ "Set off" / "set out" = start travelling.

exercises.text: "She arrived ___ the airport two hours early."
exercises.hint: "Arrive AT" + specific building/point. "She arrived AT the airport." ✅ (buildings/stations/airports = "at")

exercises.text: "I made a trip to Georgia last summer."
opts: Wrong — should be "went on a trip"
exercises.correct: Wrong — should be "went on a trip"
exercises.hint: ✅ "I WENT ON a trip to Georgia." — "go on a trip" is the correct collocation. NOT "make a trip."

exercises.text: "Rustam ___ the overnight train to save on accommodation."
exercises.hint: "TOOK the overnight train" ✅ (used it) / "BOOKED the overnight train" ✅ (reserved it). Both work in different contexts!
"travel light" = take as little luggage as possible. One backpack, no heavy suitcases. ✅

exercises.text: "Don't ___ your connection in Istanbul — the next flight isn't until tomorrow."
exercises.hint: "MISS your connection" = arrive too late to catch your connecting flight. "Don't MISS your connection!" ✅

exercises.text: "___ of your time in Almaty — there's so much to see!" (use it well)
exercises.hint: "MAKE THE MOST OF" = use something (time, opportunity) as well as possible. "Make the most of your time." ✅

questions.text: "She ___ a flight to Istanbul." Correct collocation:
questions.hint: "BOOK a flight." ✅ You book (reserve) flights, rooms, tickets.

questions.text: "They ___ a tour of the old city." Correct collocation:
questions.hint: "GO ON a tour." ✅ You go on: a tour, a trip, a holiday, an excursion.

questions.text: "We arrived ___ Almaty." Choose the correct preposition.
questions.hint: "arrive IN" + city. "We arrived IN Almaty." ✅ NEVER "arrive to." ✅

questions.text: "She arrived ___ the hotel at midnight." Choose.
questions.hint: "arrive AT" + specific building. "She arrived AT the hotel." ✅

questions.text: "We ___ early — at 4 a.m. — to drive to the airport." (begin the journey)
questions.hint: "SET OFF" = begin a journey. "We SET OFF at 4 a.m." ✅

questions.text: "I ___ the bus — it left 3 minutes ago." Choose.
questions.hint: "MISS the bus" = arrive too late to get on it. "I MISSED the bus." ✅

questions.text: "I make a trip to Shymkent." — What is wrong?
opts: "make a trip" is wrong — should be "go on a trip"
questions.correct: "make a trip" is wrong — should be "go on a trip"
questions.hint: ✅ "I WENT ON a trip to Shymkent." — "make a trip" is not a standard English collocation.
"travel light" = pack as little as possible — minimal luggage.

questions.text: "How do I ___ the station from here?"
questions.hint: "GET TO" = how do I arrive at / travel to? "How do I GET TO the station?" ✅ Informal equivalent of "arrive at."

questions.text: "Make the most of your time in Turkestan." "Make the most of" means:
opts: Use your time as well as possible
questions.correct: Use your time as well as possible
questions.hint: "make the most of" = use something (time, opportunity) to its full potential. ✅

questions.text: "He ___ the overnight train to save on accommodation." (used it)
questions.hint: "TAKE the overnight train" = use this form of transport. "He TOOK the overnight train." ✅

opts: Put belongings into luggage — prepare to leave
questions.correct: Put belongings into luggage — prepare to leave
questions.hint: "pack your bags" = put your clothes and belongings into a suitcase or bag. Ready to travel. ✅

opts: Flight that connects to your next flight
questions.correct: Flight that connects to your next flight
questions.hint: "connection" = a connecting flight or train. Miss your connection = arrive too late for the next leg of your journey.

opts: Away from typical tourist routes — unusual destination
questions.correct: Away from typical tourist routes — unusual destination
questions.hint: "off the beaten track" = not a typical tourist destination; somewhere unusual and less visited.

questions.text: "We caught a bus to the canyon." "Caught a bus" implies:
opts: Some urgency — they nearly missed it
questions.correct: Some urgency — they nearly missed it
questions.hint: "catch a bus/train" implies you ran or hurried to get it. Suggests urgency. "TAKE a bus" is neutral; "CATCH a bus" = nearly missed!

questions.text: Which sentence has the correct collocation?
questions.hint: "GO ON holiday." ✅ "She WENT ON holiday TO Georgia." — "go on" + holiday/trip/excursion.
